title: What if you lined up every planet?

narration.heading: Every planet, to scale
narration.text: You think Earth is a big planet? Wait till you see where it ranks.

narration.heading: Mercury
narration.text: Start with Mercury, the smallest planet. It's only a little bigger than our Moon.

narration.heading: Mars
narration.text: Then Mars. Red, rocky, and only about half as wide as Earth.

narration.heading: Earth
narration.text: Here's home, the biggest rocky planet there is. And Venus? It's only a little smaller.

narration.heading: The ice giants
narration.text: Now the ice giants. Neptune is about four Earths wide, and Uranus is almost its twin.

narration.heading: Saturn
narration.text: Saturn is nine Earths across. Hollow it out, and over seven hundred Earths would fit inside.

narration.heading: Jupiter
narration.text: And the king, Jupiter. Eleven Earths wide, with room for a thousand Earths inside.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? Line up every other planet side by side, and they'd fit between Earth and the Moon.

narration.heading: Room to spare?
narration.text: But only when the Moon is at its farthest. Which planet would you visit first?

hook.banner: How big are the planets, really?

skit.text: Seven planets in one gap? I can't even fit my cables in a drawer.

titles: What if you lined up every planet? (to scale)
Every planet to scale, from Mercury to Jupiter
youtube.description: A to-scale zoom out from Mercury to Mars, Earth, Neptune, Saturn and Jupiter, ending on how all the other planets could squeeze between Earth and the Moon.

sources.claim: Mercury is the smallest planet, only slightly larger than Earth's Moon; radius 2,440 km
The Moon's radius is about 1,740 km (about 3,480 km across); average distance 384,400 km
Mars has a radius of 3,390 km and is about half the size of Earth
Earth's equatorial diameter is 12,756 km; it is the biggest of the terrestrial planets
Venus is nearly as big around as Earth: 12,104 km across versus 12,756 km
Neptune's equatorial diameter is 49,528 km, about four times wider than Earth
Uranus's equatorial diameter is 51,118 km, four times wider than Earth
Saturn is about 120,500 km across, 9 times wider than Earth
Saturn's volume is 763.59 times Earth's; equatorial radius 60,268 km
Jupiter has a radius of 69,911 km, is 11 times wider than Earth, and 1,000 Earths could fit inside it
Planet diameters: Mercury 4,879 km, Mars 6,792 km, Jupiter 142,984 km, Saturn 120,536 km
The other seven planets' average diameters add up to 380,016 km; they don't fit at the Moon's average distance (about 376,000 km surface to surface) but do fit at apogee (about 398,000 km)
At the Moon's most distant, all the planets fit between Earth and the Moon
